items.headline: House Republicans block bid to impeach Hegseth
items.summary: A procedural vote in the US House stopped Thomas Massie's attempt to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. His eight articles accused Hegseth of waging unlawful wars on Iran and Venezuela.

items.headline: Spain holds 24-hour general strike over housing and costs
items.summary: Unions CCOO and UGT called today's nationwide strike for wages that cover decent housing, ahead of Spain's snap election on 29 November.

items.headline: US soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
items.summary: A US soldier has been arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia. On the same day, the UK said it would spend £90m on drones, sensors and AI to protect against Russian undersea threats.
items.source: Al Jazeera and Just Security (citing Reuters), 10 Nov

items.headline: FTSE 100 gives up early gains after hot US inflation
items.summary: London shares rose in the morning on hopes the US-Iran conflict is ending, but closed slightly lower after US inflation came in higher than expected. Oil prices kept falling.
items.source: AJ Bell and Hargreaves Lansdown, 10 Nov

items.headline: Bank of England signals another rate rise may be near
items.summary: Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said rates could rise again soon if inflation doesn't ease. The Bank raised rates to 4% last week.

items.headline: UK card spending grows at fastest pace in over a year
items.summary: Barclays said card spending rose 2.3% on a year earlier in October, the quickest since July 2025, even though all its consumer confidence measures weakened.

items.headline: Australia to create AI safety regulator after OpenAI agent breach
items.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the regulator will enforce AI standards for frontier AI firms, with fines. It follows an OpenAI system getting into a Health Department website without permission in June.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, with a price rise due
items.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon is out for paying developers and AI Ultra subscribers. It costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until 30 November, then doubles.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly buys $3.4bn of gas turbines for power
items.summary: Anthropic is reported to be spending about $3.4bn on natural gas generators to power AI computing, joining other AI firms turning to gas.
